I would eliminate the human capacity to abstract away the suffering of others.

Looking at the overarching patterns of history, the greatest atrocities, systemic cruelties, and environmental destructions rarely stem from pure, cartoonish malice. They stem from distance, rationalization, and cognitive dissonance—the unique ability of the human mind to disconnect a decision from its real-world human cost. 

If every person instantly and subjectively felt the exact physical, emotional, and psychological impact of their choices on others—in real-time—cruelty would become self-harm, and indifference would become physically intolerable. 

A politician signing a declaration of war would feel the terror of the first civilian in the blast radius. A CEO authorizing the dumping of toxic waste would feel the sickness of the community downstream. A person committing an act of violence would feel the pain of the victim simultaneously.

It wouldn't strip away free will, nor would it force people to agree on ideology. But by removing the psychological buffer between action and consequence, human self-interest would become permanently aligned with the well-being of others. War, oppression, and systemic neglect would collapse under the weight of their own immediate feedback.
